debate_title: Is current AI progress driven mainly by scaling compute, ...

conflicts.point: Whether upstream physical infrastructure controls and hardware telemetry can effectively contain foundation model capabilities or whether such measures merely cause administrative gridlock and encourage offshore migration.

positions.stance: Argues that mandatory hardware telemetry and clean-room audits are necessary upstream containment mechanisms to prevent irreversible proliferation.
Argues that hardware surveillance fails to stop software propagation while imposing severe opportunity costs on energy infrastructure and technological progress.

conflicts.point: Whether point-of-execution liability and application-layer tripwires provide sufficient governance for open-weight models once weights enter public circulation.

positions.stance: Maintains that open-weight releases permanently sever the control chain, making post-deployment liability inadequate for mitigating systemic risks.
Asserts that existing statutory authorities and point-of-execution regulations manage commercial risks more effectively than rigid hardware embargoes.

verdicts.conflict: Whether upstream physical infrastructure controls and hardware telemetry can effectively contain foundation model capabilities or whether such measures merely cause administrative gridlock and encourage offshore migration.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics anchor their arguments in concrete physical data, citing Dominion Energy figures showing three-gigawatt power requirements for hyperscale data centers that highlight the immense friction of physical infrastructure. Safetyists rely on abstract risk frameworks without providing verifiable mechanisms to prevent software migration to unmonitored jurisdictions. Consequently, the skeptic position scores higher on specificity and empirical grounding.

verdicts.conflict: Whether point-of-execution liability and application-layer tripwires provide sufficient governance for open-weight models once weights enter public circulation.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics and accelerationists account for the technical reality that open-weight models match proprietary outputs at a fraction of the cost, making upstream hardware embargoes porous. Safetyists fail to address how upstream controls retrieve weights once they enter public circulation. Therefore, downstream enforcement covers a broader and more realistic set of deployment conditions.
